note: Met 43.25.1 shouldered zun (13th c. BCE). Published H 400, rim D 352, base D 225 mm (Met API: 40.005 / 35.243 / 22.543 cm). Weight not published. Proportions measured from DP140765 (front.jpg, camera on a nose line) and DP140764 (three-quarter.jpg, camera on a mould seam); see dossier.md. THREE-FOLD vessel: 3 mould sectors of 120 deg. Axes: front (+Z, azimuth 0) = a NOSE line: belly nose flange + foot nose flange + shoulder animal head + the symmetric neck blade all sit on azimuth 0; mould seams (join flanges) at +-60 and 180. Part names (userData.part): body = the whole lathe (foot + belly + shoulder + neck + trumpet + lip, incl. low relief, eye bosses, dentils and the thin neck seam ridges), flanges = the 12 slab flanges (6 belly + 6 foot, one per register per 60 deg, each a separate mesh) + 3 low plain shoulder strips on the seams (= 15 meshes), heads = the 3 sculpted bovine heads on the shoulder at azimuths 0, 120, 240. If the shoulder strips are built inside body, set flangeCount to 12 and flangeTop to 0.61.

headSpan.note: revised from 0.75: with heads at 0 and +-120 deg the span is set by the side heads snouts (0.866 x reach); in front.jpg they reach about as far as the belly flange tips
